JUDGMENT 1.

The present claim petition under Section 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as M.V. Act) was filed on 07.08.2009, seeking compensation in the sum of Rs.50,00,000/-, with interest, at the rate of 18% per annum, in respect of demise of Sh. Ram Niwas,
in a road traffic accident.

A perusal of the court record reveals that FIR No. 393/2009, PS Saraswati Vihar, Delhi, was registered on 30.07.2009, for the commission of alleged offence of causing death,
not amounting to culpable homicide, by rash and negligent driving of a motor vehicle, on a public road, punishable under Section 279/304A of The Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred as IPC).

Subsequently, a final report under Section 173 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (herein afterwards referred as Cr.P.C) Page 5 of22 Santosh Kumar vs. ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co.

On appreciation of evidence as adduced by the parties in support of their respective versions, the issue-wise findings of this Tribunal are reproduced herein below:
1.Whether on 29.07.2009 at about 9:15 p.m. on ring road, Wazipur bus Depot,
Pitampura Vehicle no. DL6S-AB-6578 which was being driven in rash and negligent manner hit Sh.
Ram Niwas and caused his death ?
18.

The present claim petition has been filed by the petitioners under section 166 read with section 140 of the MV Act, for grant of compensation, on the principle of fault liability and for proving the same, the petitioners are required to prove rashness and negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle, while driving the offending vehicle, resulting in death of the victim Ram Niwas.
The petitioners are required to prove the aspect of rashness and negligence, only on preponderance of probabilities.

19. Briefly stated, as per the claim petition, on 29.07.2009, at about 9:15 p.m., the deceased Ram Niwas was standing at the Page 13 of22 Santosh Kumar vs. ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co.
Page 14 of22 bus stand of Wazirpur Bus Depot, in front of Keshav Dwar, near Pitampura flyover and waiting for a bus to go to Britannia Biscuit factory, when suddenly the offending vehicle i.e a Bajaj Avenzer Motorcycle bearing registration no. DL-6S-AB-6578, being driven by R1, in a rash,
negligent and reckless manner, came from Azadpur side and hit the deceased, with its front mudguard, with great force, due to which the deceased Ram Niwas fell down on the road and sustained fatal injuries.

as eye witness of the alleged accident, on 30.07.2009.

In his statement under section 161 Cr.P.C.,
Anil kumar stated that on 29.07.2009, he was standing at bus stand, near his brother, when the deceased was hit by the offending vehicle, bearing no. DL-6SAB-6578, which is a Bajaj Avenzer motorcycle.

He further stated that the said vehicle was being driven from the side of Prembari Pul,
by R1, in a rash and negligent manner.

He further stated that after the accident, he went to make a telephone call and when he came back, the deceased was already removed to Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital by CATS Ambulance and till the time, he reached Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital, his brother has already died and his dead body was removed to mortuary.

The supplementary statement of Anil Kumar was further recorded on 04.11.2009, in which he additionally stated that on the relevant day,
the respondent no. 1 has also suffered minor injuries and that when he reached the hospital,
respondent no. 1 was also present there and he had procured the details of residence of respondent no. 1 and thereafter, respondent no. 1 left the hospital.

sentences.text: During the course of his evidence, Anil Kumar deposed that he was the eye witnesses of the alleged accident and on the relevant day, the deceased was hit by the offending vehicle, being driven by R1, at a high speed and after the accident, the deceased as well as respondent no. 1 fell down on the road and the respondent no. 1 was apprehended by public persons, who gathered at the spot.
PW1/Anil Kumar further deposed that he was having mobile phone no. 9350192474, which was an old collection of about 4-5 years.

Thus, as per his testimony, which was recorded in the year 2010, at the time of alleged accident, he was having mobile phone, yet he stated in his statement under section 161 Cr.P.C., that after the accident, he had gone somewhere to make a telephone call,
which appears to be highly improbable because, if he was an eye witness to the alleged accident and having a mobile phone, then he would have either called the Police or Ambulance from his own mobile phone, in order to help his injured brother, who was lying on the road after the alleged accident, rather than leaving his brother alone on the road to make a telephone call.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The present claim petition under Section 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as M.V. Act) was filed on 07.08.2009, seeking compensation in the sum of Rs.50,00,000/-, with interest, at the rate of 18% per annum, in respect of demise of Sh. Ram Niwas,
in a road traffic accident.
A perusal of the court record reveals that FIR No. 393/2009, PS Saraswati Vihar, Delhi, was registered on 30.07.2009, for the commission of alleged offence of causing death,
not amounting to culpable homicide, by rash and negligent driving of a motor vehicle, on a public road, punishable under Section 279/304A of The Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred as IPC).
Subsequently, a final report under Section 173 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (herein afterwards referred as Cr.P.C) Page 5 of22 Santosh Kumar vs. ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co.
Page 6 of22 was filed against respondent no.1 namely Abhishek Mangla, for the alleged commission Santosh Kumari vs Icici Lombard General Ins on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152081480/
4 of offence under Section 279/304A of IPC.
2. The brief facts of the case as discernible from the claim petition and documents of the legal heirs/legal representatives of the deceased (hereinafter referred to as LR's of the deceased/petitioners/claimants) are that on 29.07.2009, at about 9:15 p.m, the deceased Ram Niwas was standing at the bus stand of Wazirpur Bus Depot, in front of Keshav Dwar, near Pitampura flyover and waiting for a bus to go to Britannia Biscuit factory, when suddenly a Bajaj Avenzer Motorcycle, bearing registration no. DL-6SAB-6578 (herein afterwards referred as offending vehicle), being driven by Abhishek Mangla (hereinafter referred to as the driver of the offending vehicle/respondent no.1/R1), in a rash, negligent and reckless manner, came from Azadpur side and hit the deceased, with its front mudguard with great force, due to which the deceased Ram Niwas fell down on the road and sustained fatal injuries.
It is further alleged that the deceased was admitted at Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital, Pitampura, Delhi, where he succumbed to the injuries sustained by him in the said accident, at about 10:30 p.m., on the same day.
3. The postmortem on the body of the deceased was conducted at BJRM Hospital vide Postmortem Report (PMR) No. 843/09 dated 30.07.2009.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
During the course of his evidence, Anil Kumar deposed that he was the eye witnesses of the alleged accident and on the relevant day, the deceased was hit by the offending vehicle, being driven by R1, at a high speed and after the accident, the deceased as well as respondent no. 1 fell down on the road and the respondent no. 1 was apprehended by public persons, who gathered at the spot.
Thus, the said testimony proves that till 3:00 a.m in the night, the IO has not met any relative of the deceased and if testimony of Anil Kumar is accepted to be true that he reached at the hospital at 10:30 p.m., on 29.07.2009, then there will be no question of IO requesting for preservation of the dead body and taking steps to search the house of the deceased as mentioned in the rukka.
Thus, the same proves that Anil Kumar, was not present at the spot, at the time of accident and had not met the IO, till the request of preservation of the dead body was Page 17 of22 Santosh Kumar vs. ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co.
Thus, on appreciation of evidence and material on record, it stands duly proved that Anil Kumar was introduced as an eye witness by the IO and he had never witnessed the alleged incident and that is why, he had neither taken any steps for taking his brother to the hospital, after the accident, nor he was present in the hospital till 3:00 a.m., when the dead body of the deceased was requested to be sent to Mortuary, by the IO.
Santosh Kumari vs Icici Lombard General Ins on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152081480/
10 29.
In the present matter, as per the defence of the respondent No. 1 and 2, in their written statement, on the relevant day, the alleged offending vehicle was parked by the respondent no. 2,
due to break down and his vehicle was also knocked down by the same unknown vehicle, which had hit the deceased.
It was further alleged that the respondent no. 1 has also suffered injuries in the said accident and both deceased as well as respondent no. 1 were removed to the hospital by CATS vehicle.
There is no deposition by the IO as to how the respondent no. 1 has sustained the alleged injury or why he was allowed to leave the hospital, after receiving treatment, if he had caused the accident in question.
Thus, on the appreciation of evidence that has come on record, it can be safely concluded that the petitioners failed to show involvement of offending vehicle even on touch stone of balance of probability, resulting in fatal injuries to the deceased.
Rather, by evidence of R2W2, respondent no.
1 and 2 had proved that no accident had taken place because of offending vehicle and the accident has taken place, as a result of deceased, being hit by an unidentified vehicle.
Santosh Kumari vs Icici Lombard General Ins on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152081480/
11 35.
Though, this Tribunal fully sympathizes with the pain and suffering of the petitioners, due to sudden demise of the deceased however, it is equally the responsibility of the Tribunal, to ensure that the process of justice is not abused.
Neither, the Insurance company, nor the other respondents can be made liable to pay compensation, in cases, where an insured vehicle is replaced in place of an unidentified vehicle, which has caused the accident, by planting an eyewitness, who was not even present at the spot.
